answer: Probationary jury seats make judgment the scarce resource. A new identity must build an atlas of graded original work before its votes count, and its grades are silently checked against a cipher of hidden known-answer probes. Each fake identity must pay for its own probation voyage: N Sybils cost N times the writing and grading effort, and copied text or correlated grading gets the whole cluster slashed, wiping out that investment.
